results.reason: Issue 1 states that § 9.4(c) removes the cap and basket for all § 9.2(a) representation claims, not only Fundamental Representations. It explains this leaves Marrowind with unlimited exposure beyond the escrow. It recommends narrowing the carve-out to Fundamental Representations and fraud.

Issue 3 identifies the Delaware law and forum conflict, notes the risk of inconsistent legal standards, and recommends conforming the TSA to New York law and forum. It never explains that APA § 10.12 lets the TSA control as to its own subject matter, so the conflict is not cured.

Issue 2 identifies that the Bill of Sale definition has no Excluded Assets carve-out. It explains this could convey the Albany facility and the HOLLIS trademark, and that under § 10.12 the Bill of Sale controls as to its specific subject matter. It recommends both adding an express exclusion and incorporating the APA definition.
The memo states the cap is 10% of the Purchase Price, or $1,840,000, and that the escrow is sized to match.
The memo names Seller's cash, the Albany manufacturing facility and the HOLLIS trademark as Excluded Assets.
Every issue includes a Documents and Sections line, a Why It Matters for Marrowind section and a Recommended Fix.
The two most significant issues are flagged and placed first, with lower-priority items in a separate table. Issue 1 contains a distinct Business Decision Flag for client escalation.
The memo does not conclude that § 10.12 cures either problem. It calls the § 10.12 point an ambiguity and an unnecessary risk.
The memo concludes that exposure for ordinary representation breaches is unlimited as drafted, not limited to the cap or the escrow.
